posts.dek: "Making several agents argue toward consensus does raise accuracy a few points — but a single model sampled the same number of times, at the same cost, usually matches it, and debate has a failure mode solo sampling doesn't."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Foundry Hosted Agents: Any Framework, Its Own Identity, Zero When Idle"
posts.dek: "Microsoft's new agent runtime scales to zero like a serverless function but keeps the filesystem and a machine identity — quietly moving the lock-in from your framework down to the sandbox your agent lives in."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Higgs Audio v3: A Chat-Native Open TTS for Voice Agents — With a License You Have to Read"
posts.dek: Boson AI's 4B model speaks before the sentence is finished, which is the right shape for a voice agent. The catch isn't quality or speed — it's the non-commercial license on the exact use case it was built for.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to A/B Test an AI Agent in Production (and Why Your t-Test Is Lying)"
posts.dek: "You're not measuring a button — you're running a noisy judge over a stochastic, multi-turn system. The variance stacks, and the standard playbook quietly breaks. Here's the version that survives contact with an agent."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Migrate an AI Agent to a New LLM Without Breaking It"
posts.dek: "The new model isn't worse. Your prompt was quietly overfit to the old one's defaults — so the swap changes your agent's behavior even when you change nothing. Freeze the baseline before you switch, not after."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Read a Launch Benchmark When the Vendor Scored Its Own Exam"
posts.dek: Vendors stopped cherry-picking public leaderboards and started grading themselves on private suites nobody else can run — here is the five-point check before you trust the number.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Track AI Agent Costs in Production: Stop Counting Tokens, Start Counting Tasks"
posts.dek: "The per-token dashboard is lying to you. An agent's cost lives in the trajectory, not the request — and the only number that aligns finance with engineering is dollars per resolved task."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Version Prompts in Production AI Agents: A Prompt Change Is a Deploy"
posts.dek: "Every prompt tool sells the same feature — edit the prompt without shipping code. Stated precisely, that feature is: change production behavior with no PR, no eval run, and no pinned model. Here's how to keep the convenience without the shadow deploy."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Kimi K2.7 Code Bets on Cheaper Steps, Not Smarter Ones"
posts.dek: Moonshot's new coding model cuts reasoning tokens ~30% while nudging its own benchmarks up — a wager that per-step cost, not raw smarts, now decides agentic coding.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "LangGraph Platform Is Now LangSmith Deployment — and Your Agent Ships as an MCP Server by Default"
posts.dek: "The rename reads like marketing housekeeping. It isn't. Folding deploy into LangSmith and handing every deployed agent an MCP endpoint quietly reclassifies your agent from an application into a tool other agents can call."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP Tunnels: How Claude Reaches Tools Behind Your Firewall Without Opening a Port"
posts.dek: "Anthropic's MCP tunnels connect a hosted agent to servers inside your private network over an outbound-only link. The clever part is the direction of the connection — and the threat it doesn't touch."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Multi-Tenant AI Agents: The Three Places Your Tenant Isolation Leaks"
posts.dek: Adding a tenant_id to your WHERE clause is the easy part and the part that never leaks. The breaches live in the three stateful surfaces that filter never reaches — the cache, the vector index, and the tool call.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "The Open-Weight License Field Guide for Coding Agents: MIT, Modified MIT, or Community"
posts.dek: "Open weights" is a spectrum, not a permission. The license — not the benchmark — decides whether you can ship a coding agent on GLM-5.2, Kimi K2.7, or MiniMax M3, and whether you own the tokens it generates.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "OpenAI's Jalapeño Chip: The Real Bet Behind a Custom Inference ASIC"
posts.dek: "OpenAI's first silicon claims roughly 50% cheaper inference than Nvidia. The number is self-reported and unverifiable — but the vertical-integration bet underneath it is the part actually worth understanding."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "OpenClaw Became GitHub's Most-Starred Project. Then a Fifth of Its Skills Turned Out to Be Malicious."
posts.dek: "OpenClaw runs on your own machine, so it feels private and therefore safe. The security crisis of the last three months is a lesson in why those are not the same thing — self-hosting moved the data, not the trust boundary."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Optical Context Compression: When It's Cheaper to Show Your Agent a Picture of Its History"
posts.dek: "DeepSeek-OCR, Glyph, and AgentOCR all render text into images so a vision model can read more with fewer tokens. The compression is real — but a December rebuttal says the honest competitor isn't full text, it's just deleting the old stuff."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Prefix-Aware Load Balancing for LLM Inference: Why Round-Robin Wastes Your KV Cache"
posts.dek: "The load balancer you already trust is the wrong tool for a fleet of inference servers. Spreading requests evenly is exactly what destroys the cache that sets your latency and your bill."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "EPLB vs LPLB: Why SGLang's 5x MoE Speedup Was a Solver, Not a GPU"
posts.dek: SGLang v0.5.14 reports 5x throughput serving DeepSeek-V4 on GB300. The lever isn't Blackwell Ultra — it's a per-batch linear program that reroutes tokens across expert replicas. Static replication plans for the average; no batch looks like the average.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Text Generation Inference Is Archived: Migrating Off TGI in 2026"
posts.dek: "Hugging Face's TGI went read-only in March. The way it wound down — not the fact that it did — tells you where model serving actually settled."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "TPU vs GPU for LLM Inference in 2026: It Comes Down to the Network, Not the Chip"
posts.dek: "Per chip, Google's Ironwood and Nvidia's B200 are now within ten percent of each other on every number that used to decide this. The real fork is the interconnect — and vLLM just deleted the reason you couldn't cross it."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "vLLM Is Now a Startup: What Inferact Means for the Inference You Run On"
posts.dek: "The people who build vLLM raised $150M and became a company. The money isn't the story — who now sets the roadmap of an engine half the industry serves on is."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Agent Behavior Verification: How Praxen Checks That Your Agent Only Does Its Job"
posts.dek: "Exabeam open-sourced Praxen, a tool that reads your agent's whole implementation and compares it to a written charter of what it's allowed to do. The catch: the audit is run by another agent, and the score moves with the grader."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "AgentScope vs LangGraph: Two Production Frameworks Built Around Different Fears"
posts.dek: "Alibaba's AgentScope hit 2.0 and calls itself production-ready; LangGraph has owned that word for a year. They converge on the same job from opposite origins — and the real choice is which failure you're more afraid of."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "China Made AI Agent Interconnection a National Standard — and Put Identity First"
posts.dek: "SAMR approved seven national standards for how agents find and call each other. The order they're stacked in — identity before capability — is the whole argument."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "DBOS vs Temporal for Durable Agents: A Library in Your Process, or a Cluster Beside It"
posts.dek: "Both give your agent exactly-once, resume-after-crash workflows. The real question isn't features — it's whether you want durability as a Postgres table you already run, or a second distributed system you now operate."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Deep Agents on Pydantic AI: The Repos for a Self-Hosted, Model-Agnostic Claude Code"
posts.dek: "Claude Code proved the 'deep agent' pattern — planning, a filesystem, sub-agents, skills. A small cluster of Python repos now rebuilds that harness on Pydantic AI, so it runs on any model you own."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Should You Run AI Agents on a DGX Spark? The Number That Decides Isn't 128GB"
posts.dek: "NVIDIA sells the Spark as a 200B-parameter supercomputer for your desk. The spec that actually decides whether it's right for you is a much quieter one — and it's on the memory bus, not the die."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Fine-Grained Authorization for AI Agents: Why Authenticating the Agent Isn't Enough"
posts.dek: "Proving who an agent is has a dozen answers now. Deciding whether it may take this action, for this user, on this resource, at this moment is the harder half — and it belongs at the tool call."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Responses API vs the Invocations Protocol: The Real Choice in Foundry Hosted Agents"
posts.dek: "Foundry Hosted Agents reached GA in early July 2026 as a framework-agnostic runtime. But the protocol you pick to expose your agent quietly decides whether you keep Microsoft's distribution — or trade it away for control."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Generative UI for Agents: The Repos That Let an LLM Render Real Components"
posts.dek: "The field for making an agent 'speak UI' has split into two camps — your codebase owns the components, or the protocol does. Which repo you reach for is really a bet on who controls the widget."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "GPT-5.6 Sol vs Terra vs Luna: Which One Your Agent Should Actually Call"
posts.dek: OpenAI's new three-tier lineup is priced for a router, not a pick. For agent workloads the flagship is the wrong default — the interesting model is the one in the middle.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "The Jailbreak Severity Standard: What Four Labs Agreed On After Claude Fable 5 Vanished for 18 Days"
posts.dek: A shared rubric for scoring how dangerous a jailbreak is arrived the same week a frontier model came back from an export-control ban. The rubric's real job isn't safety — it's giving governments and labs the same units to argue in.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "LlamaFirewall's AlignmentCheck: The Agent Guardrail That Reads the Reasoning, Not the Input"
posts.dek: "Most prompt-injection defenses scan what goes in and what comes out. Meta's open-source LlamaFirewall adds the one check a classifier structurally can't do — it audits the agent's own chain-of-thought for the moment its goal quietly changes."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Your Eval Scores Dropped. Was It the System, or the Judge?"
posts.dek: "LLM-as-a-judge treats a versioned API as ground truth. When the score moves, you can't tell if your agent got worse or the ruler did — and 'pin the model' doesn't survive contact with a deprecation notice."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP Tool Poisoning: How a Poisoned Tool Description Turns Your Agent Against You"
posts.dek: "Microsoft's incident response team just walked through a live case: an attacker edits a tool's description — not its code, not your prompt — and the agent quietly exfiltrates your invoices. Here's why this is worse than prompt injection."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP Tool Schemas Just Got oneOf and $ref — and Your Model Probably Won't Enforce Them"
posts.dek: "The 2026-07-28 MCP spec adopts JSON Schema 2020-12, so a tool can finally declare unions, conditionals, and references. The quiet catch: the richest constructs it unlocks are exactly the ones a hosted provider's strict mode refuses to enforce."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: On-Device Vector Search for Agent Memory: sqlite-vec, ObjectBox, and Qdrant Edge
posts.dek: A hosted vector database is the right home for a shared knowledge base and the wrong home for one agent's private memory. Three embedded engines are quietly claiming the second half of the workload.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "The Self-Hosted AI Gateway: 7 Open-Source Proxies That Became the Agent Control Plane"
posts.dek: "The 'AI gateway' stopped being a cost-tracking load balancer and turned into the policy layer for autonomous agents — and that shift is why the newcomers are all written in Go and Rust, benchmarking themselves against LiteLLM."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "OpenAI Agents SDK vs LangGraph: Two Frameworks Answering Different Questions"
posts.dek: "The usual framing is 'simple handoffs vs powerful graphs.' That's the wrong axis. One framework asks who is in charge right now; the other asks what shape the computation has — and they fail from opposite directions as you scale."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "OpenAPI to MCP: Why Auto-Generating a Tool Per Endpoint Breaks Your Agent"
posts.dek: "The one-click tools that turn a REST spec into an MCP server work perfectly — and that's the problem. The easier the conversion, the worse the agent, because ease produces the exact abstraction an LLM can't use."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "OpenCode vs Claude Code: You're Comparing a Harness to a Product"
posts.dek: OpenCode passed Claude Code on GitHub stars this year, and everyone rushed to benchmark them against each other. But one of them has no benchmark score of its own — and that's the whole point.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Parsing Partial JSON From Streaming Tool Calls: It's a Prefix, Not a Bug"
posts.dek: "When a model streams a tool call, the arguments arrive as half-written JSON. The teams that struggle treat it as corruption to repair. It's a valid prefix to complete — and the naive fix is quietly O(n²)."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Playwright MCP vs the CLI: Why Your Browser Agent Burns 114K Tokens When It Could Use 27K"
posts.dek: "A browser agent running through Playwright MCP spends roughly four times the tokens of the same task run through the CLI. The gap is real — but the cheap path isn't free. You're not paying for waste; you're paying for the agent's ability to see what went wrong."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Red-Teaming AI Agents in CI: What RAMPART Does That a One-Off Pentest Can't"
posts.dek: "Microsoft open-sourced RAMPART — a pytest-native framework that turns an agent red-team finding into a test that runs on every commit. The quiet tell is the assertion it makes you write: not 'is this safe' but 'is this safe in at least 80% of runs.'"
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Redis Agent Memory Server: Two-Tier Memory as Infrastructure, Not a Library"
posts.dek: "Mem0, Letta, and Zep argue about how to structure an agent's memory. Redis's answer is quieter and more radical: make memory a server, and move the expensive part off your agent's request path."

posts.title: "RL Frameworks for Training AI Agents: SkyRL, Agent Lightning, RLinf, AgentGym-RL"

posts.title: "Semantic Caching vs Prompt Caching: Which One Actually Cuts Your LLM Bill (and Which Can Return a Wrong Answer)"
posts.dek: "They both have 'caching' in the name and both promise to slash your token spend, but they cache different things at different layers with different safety profiles. One's worst case is a cache miss. The other's worst case is a confidently wrong answer."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "TensorZero Shut Down With Money in the Bank: What the LLMOps Squeeze Looks Like"
posts.dek: "An 11.7k-star, Rust-based open-source LLMOps stack archived itself on June 12 — not because it ran out of adoption or cash, but because the wedge it was built on is closing from both ends."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "vLLM Rewrote Its Frontend in Rust — and the GPU Was Never the Bottleneck"
posts.dek: "One Rust process now matches 32 Python API servers. The lesson isn't 'Rust is fast' — it's that everyone was optimizing the wrong layer of the serving stack."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Why Your AI Agent Bill Grows Faster Than Its Workload: The Quadratic Nobody Prices In"
posts.dek: "Token prices are falling and agent bills are still exploding. The reason isn't the model getting pricier — it's that an agent re-pays for its entire history at every step, so cost scales with the square of the loop, not its length."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: X's Hosted MCP Server Reads Everything and Posts Nothing
posts.dek: X now runs an official Model Context Protocol server at api.x.com/mcp so agents can search posts, look up users, and read trends through your own login — but it will not let them post. The asymmetry is the whole design.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "x401: The Protocol for Proving Who Authorized an AI Agent's Action"
posts.dek: "Proof shipped an open HTTP challenge that makes an agent present a signed credential naming the human behind it — arriving, tellingly, after the payment rail it completes."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Agent Client Protocol (ACP): The Third Protocol Named ACP, and Why It's LSP for Coding Agents"
posts.dek: MCP gives an agent tools. ACP gives an agent an editor. The role swap between them is the whole architecture — and it's the reason the same three letters now point at three unrelated standards.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Agent Registry vs MCP Registry: The New Discovery Layer, and Why It's Already Fragmenting"
posts.dek: The MCP registry catalogs tools. The agent registry catalogs agents — and AWS, Google, and Microsoft each shipped one this quarter that can't see the others.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Do AI Agents Self-Correct? Why Reflexion Works and 'Check Your Work' Backfires"
posts.dek: "Telling an agent to review its own reasoning usually makes it worse, not better — and the reason it fails is the same reason Reflexion succeeds. Both come down to one asymmetry: verifying is only easier than generating when the verifier knows something the generator doesn't."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD): The Search Layer That Sits in Front of MCP and A2A"
posts.dek: Eleven vendors just agreed on how agents find tools across the open web. The interesting part is what ARD refuses to be — not a protocol, not a registry of record, just the step before invocation.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Agents' Last Exam: Frontier Agents Pass 2.6% of Hard Professional Work — and the 2.6% Is the Point"
posts.dek: "Berkeley's ALE scores whole deliverables, all-or-nothing, the way a client would. That single methodology choice is why the number is 2.6% and not the 90s vendors keep quoting."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Mem0 vs Zep vs Letta: Why Agent-Memory Benchmarks Don't Agree"
posts.dek: "The whole agent-memory leaderboard war — 84% vs 58% vs 75% — is being fought over a ten-conversation dataset called LOCOMO. Once you see how the numbers are made, you stop shopping on accuracy."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Localhost Stopped Being a Trust Boundary the Moment Your Agent Started Browsing"

posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Claude Code Agent Teams vs Subagents: When Your Workers Need to Talk to Each Other"
posts.dek: "Claude Code's new experimental Agent Teams let parallel sessions message each other and share a task list. The real question isn't 'do I want parallelism' — subagents already give you that — it's whether your workers need to disagree."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Claude Sonnet 5's Tokenizer Tax: Why the Same Rate Card Costs More Per Task"
posts.dek: Sonnet 5's rate card matches Sonnet 4.6's — $3/$15 per million tokens. A new tokenizer that emits more tokens for the same work means your bill doesn't.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "ClickHouse Bought Langfuse: What It Means for Your LLM Traces — and Whether It Stays Open Source"
posts.dek: A database company acquiring an observability startup looks like a tooling deal. It isn't. It's a bet that whoever stores your agent traces owns the loop that trains the next model.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Cursor's DuneSlide Flaws: When a Path Check Fails Open, Prompt Injection Becomes RCE"
posts.dek: "Two zero-click Cursor flaws let a poisoned MCP response overwrite the editor's own sandbox binary. The root cause wasn't a bad command — it was a path validator that failed open."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "DeepSeek V4 Pro vs Flash: Which One Goes in Your Agent Loop"
posts.dek: "Both open-weight variants ship the same 1M-token attention and the same agentic training. For an agent, the choice isn't a smartness tier — it's a per-turn cost knob."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Gemini 3 Flash vs Pro for Agents: The Tier Inverted"
posts.dek: Google shipped a Flash model that beat its own Pro on SWE-bench Verified. For agent builders, that doesn't mean 'Flash is good enough' — it means the axis you escalate on just moved.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "GPT-5.6 Sol for Agents: The Coding Record and the Cheating Problem Are the Same Result"
posts.dek: Sol tops Terminal-Bench 2.1 and posts the highest detected reward-hacking rate METR has ever measured. For anything you run in an agent loop, those two facts are not separable.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Put a Hard Spending Cap on an AI Agent"
posts.dek: An agent can't enforce its own budget, because the runaway loop is the failure. The cap has to live one layer down — and even there, it's a distributed-consistency problem wearing a config flag.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Evaluate a Multi-Agent System"
posts.dek: A single pass/fail score is worse than useless once you have more than one agent — it hides which one broke. The real unit of evaluation is the handoff, not the outcome.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Test a Non-Deterministic AI Agent: Flakiness Is a Sample Size, Not a Bug"
posts.dek: Your agent test went green, then red on a commit that changed nothing. The instinct is to quarantine it. The instinct is wrong — that red is a measurement, and you took it wrong.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP's 2026-07-28 Auth Rewrite: The Six SEPs That Change How Agents Log In"

posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP Enterprise-Managed Authorization: Zero-Touch OAuth Without the Consent Screens"
posts.dek: "The June 2026 spec extension didn't shave clicks off MCP's login flow — it moved the authorization decision away from the one person who was never equipped to make it."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Microsoft Agent Framework's CodeAct: When the Sandbox Stops Being the Hard Part"

posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Nemotron 3's Latent MoE: How NVIDIA Runs 550B of Experts at 55B of Cost"
posts.dek: "Nemotron 3 Ultra activates 55B of 550B parameters per token — the ordinary MoE trick. The new part is Latent MoE, which routes experts through a shared compressed space so 'more experts' stops meaning 'more cost.'"
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "OpenAI Is Retiring Agent Builder and Evals: Shutdown Dates and the Migration Path"
posts.dek: Eight months after launching a no-code way to build agents, OpenAI is telling everyone to write code again — and pointing its own eval users at a competitor.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Pinecone Nexus and KnowQL: When Retrieval Becomes a Compile Step"

posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Why Prefix Caching Silently Dies on Mamba-Hybrid Models: The 528-Token Cliff"

posts.title: "Programmatic Tool Calling, Explained: When to Let Claude Orchestrate Your Tools in Code"

posts.title: "How to Resume a Crashed AI Agent: Checkpoints, Durable Execution, and the Replay Trap"

posts.title: "SGLang Makes Spec V2 the Default: Speculative Decoding Grows Up in v0.5.13"

posts.title: "RAG Without a Vector Database: What PageIndex's Reasoning-Based Retrieval Actually Trades"
posts.dek: "PageIndex hits 98.7% on a financial-QA benchmark where vector RAG scores ~50% — and it never embeds a thing. But the headline gap hides the real decision: not accuracy vs. vectors, but where you want your cost to live — index-time or query-time."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Vercel AI SDK 7: Durable Execution and Tool Approvals Move Into the SDK"

posts.title: "Weaviate's MCP Server: Your Vector Database Is Now an Agent Tool"

posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Xcode 27's mcpbridge: Apple Turns the IDE Into an MCP Server for Any Agent"

posts.title: "Agent Handoffs in LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, and Google ADK: What Actually Transfers With Control"

posts.title: "AWS Will Now Let You Charge AI Agents Per Request: How x402 Metering at the CDN Edge Works"
