posts.title: "Batch API vs Real-Time Inference: The 50% Discount Isn't Why You Should Use It"
posts.dek: "Every provider now sells the same deal — hand over your requests, wait up to 24 hours, pay half. The savings are real, but the reason to reach for batch is the thing nobody puts on the pricing page."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "What Anthropic's 'Dreaming' Does to Agent Memory — and Why a Bad Dream Doesn't Wash Out"
posts.dek: "Claude's new consolidation loop replays an agent's day and writes down what it learned. The same mechanism that lifted one customer's task completion ~6x is the one that makes a poisoned lesson permanent."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Claude Sonnet 5 vs Opus 4.8 for Agents: The Cheaper Model and the Tokenizer Catch"
posts.dek: "Sonnet 5 lands at 40% below Opus and beats it on terminal work — but a new tokenizer quietly inflates every token count by ~30%, so the rate card is not the price. Do the cost math in your own units."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Does Structured Output Hurt LLM Accuracy? The Format Tax, Measured"
posts.dek: "Forcing JSON can cost a reasoning model 10–15% — but the tax is paid during thinking, not from structure itself. The fix is where you put the reasoning, not whether you constrain."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Google Open-Sourced an Agent Memory System With No Vector Database. Read the Design."
posts.dek: "A Google PM's 'Always On Memory Agent' stores everything in SQLite and consolidates it with an LLM every 30 minutes. The 30-minute number tells you exactly what it's for — and what it isn't."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How MCP Servers Actually Ship: The Registry Is a Phone Book, OCI Is the Supply Chain"
posts.dek: "The official MCP registry deliberately refuses to host code — so the hard part, trust, lands wherever the artifact lives. Docker's answer is to make that place an OCI image."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Enforce a Token Budget on an AI Agent (Not Just Measure It)"
posts.dek: "Most 'agent budgets' are alerts wearing a brake's uniform: they tell you after the money is gone. Real enforcement is a prediction problem, because the cost of the next step is a bound you can only ever estimate — never a number you can look up."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Interleaved Thinking: When Should an AI Agent Reason Between Tool Calls?"
posts.dek: The point of thinking between tool calls isn't a smarter first plan — a model can plan up front without it. The point is that the model can notice a tool returned something wrong and re-plan on the spot, instead of barreling ahead.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "LangMem vs Mem0: Memory You Program vs Memory You Call"
posts.dek: "They get compared like rivals, but one is memory you program and the other is memory you call — and the benchmark leaderboard only measures one of them."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "LLM Cascade vs Router: Escalate to a Bigger Model, or Route Around It?"
posts.dek: A router picks a model before it sees the answer; a cascade tries the cheap one first and escalates only if a judge says so — and that judge, not the models, decides whether you actually save.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "The Mastra npm Attack: AI Agent Frameworks Are the New Supply-Chain Target"
posts.dek: "A North Korean crew republished 140+ Mastra packages in 88 minutes with a poisoned dependency. The scary part isn't the payload — it's that the whole attack ran before any of your agent's guardrails woke up."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP's Stateless Spec Fixes Session Hijacking — and Hands You Three New Attack Surfaces"
posts.dek: The 2026-07-28 revision closes the holes the protocol used to own. The same three headline features quietly relocate the security burden onto server code that mostly doesn't exist yet.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP Is Deprecating Sampling, Roots, and Logging: What the 2026-07-28 Spec Cuts and Why"
posts.dek: "The stateless rewrite got the headlines, but the quieter change is the one that tells you what MCP has decided to be. Three original primitives are on the way out — and they're the exact three where the server reached back into your runtime."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MiniMax M3: Frontier Coding and 1M Context on Open Weights — Read the Latency, Not the Leaderboard"
posts.dek: M3 claims to beat GPT-5.5 on SWE-bench Pro while running weights you can host yourself. The benchmark row is the least trustworthy thing in the release — and the architecture is the most.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "The NSA's MCP Security Guidance: The First Advice That Defends Against Your Own Agent"
posts.dek: "The NSA's Security Design Considerations for MCP reads like every other threat list until you notice its signature control points the wrong way — at the outbound wire, not the untrusted server. That inversion is the whole document."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Pi's System Prompt Is Under 1,000 Tokens: The Case Against Heavy Coding-Agent Harnesses"
posts.dek: "Most coding agents open with a ~10,000-token system prompt. Pi opens with under 1,000 and lets the model write its own tools. The bet underneath: the model already knows how to be an agent, and every instruction token is a task token you don't get back."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Pydantic AI V2 Is Out: What 'Capabilities' and the Harness Actually Change"
posts.dek: "V2 went stable on June 23 after seven betas, then shipped four releases in nine days. The real news isn't the version bump — it's a bet that the winning agent abstraction is a harness, not a graph."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "The Best Small Model for Your Agent Isn't the Smallest — or the Smartest"
posts.dek: "Qwen3-4B, Phi-4-mini, Gemma, Nemotron 3 Nano: the pick forks on a question no leaderboard prints — are you short on memory or short on tokens-per-dollar? And the score that decides an agent isn't MMLU."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Faithfulness vs Groundedness vs Correctness: Which RAG Hallucination Check Catches a Wrong Answer"
posts.dek: "A faithfulness score of 1.0 doesn't mean your RAG answer is right. It means the model didn't stray from the context — even when the context was wrong. Here's what each check actually audits."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Stainless Is Winding Down: Where to Generate SDKs and MCP Servers Now"
posts.dek: "The two best independent SDK generators got bought in 2026 — Fern by Postman, Stainless by Anthropic, which is retiring its shared generator. The layer that turns an API into agent-usable tools stopped being neutral infrastructure."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Text-to-SQL Accuracy in 2026: Why the Benchmark Says 90% and Your Warehouse Says 40%"
posts.dek: "Top systems clear 90% on academic SQL benchmarks and 30–60% on real enterprise warehouses. The gap isn't the model's syntax — it's your schema. And the leaderboards are half wrong."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "vLLM vs SGLang vs LMDeploy: Picking a Self-Hosted Inference Engine in 2026"
posts.dek: "With TGI archived and Hugging Face pointing everyone at vLLM and SGLang, the open-source serving field narrowed to three real choices. They hit nearly the same throughput ceiling from opposite directions — so speed is not the thing you're actually picking."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Zero Trust for AI Agents: Why the New Frameworks Treat Your Agent as an Insider Threat"
posts.dek: "Anthropic and Google DeepMind converged on the same uncomfortable premise in 2026: the agent already has legitimate credentials, so the honest security model assumes it's compromised and bounds what it can do — not whether it can get in."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How Many Tokens Does an Agent Memory Layer Use? From 7K to 3.26M per Query"
posts.dek: "A June 2026 paper clocks three popular memory frameworks on the same benchmark: 118K, 632K, and 3.26M tokens per query. The 500x spread isn't noise — it's a design choice most teams never realize they're making."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "AI Agent Goal Drift: Why Long-Running Agents Quietly Abandon the Task You Gave Them"
posts.dek: "The failure isn't that the agent forgets the goal. It's that, step by step, a louder goal replaces it — and the fix is a ratio, not a bigger memory."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "AI Agents Are Finding Real Zero-Days at Scale — and Drowning Maintainers in Fake Ones"
posts.dek: "An autonomous agent found 21 genuine zero-days in FFmpeg for about $1,000. The same technology just made curl kill its bug bounty. Discovery got cheap; disposition didn't."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Why AI Browsers Still Can't Stop Prompt Injection"
posts.dek: Nearly a year after the first Comet and Atlas exploits, the browsers' own makers say prompt injection may never be fully solved. The reason is structural, not a bug waiting for a patch.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "When \"Trust This Folder\" Means Remote Code Execution: The Amazon Q Flaw Every Coding Agent Shipped"
posts.dek: "Amazon Q auto-ran an MCP config out of any repo you opened, with your live AWS keys in the process. It got a CVE. The identical bug in Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Copilot got declared working-as-designed — because the trust prompt you inherited from your editor was never a consent to run code."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Brute-Force vs Approximate Vector Search: Do You Even Need a Vector Database?"
posts.dek: "Approximate nearest-neighbor search is a tax you pay to survive scale you may not have. Below a few hundred thousand vectors, exact brute-force is faster, perfectly accurate, and has no index to rot."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Context Compaction Is Quietly Deleting Your Agent's Guardrails"
posts.dek: "The summary your long-running agent writes to stay under its token budget is lossy in one direction: it keeps the rules that fire and drops the rules that forbid. New research puts a number on how fast safety erodes."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Cross-Cluster LLM Serving: Why KServe, llm-d, and Dynamo Stop at the Cluster Line"
posts.dek: The Kubernetes-native serving stack got very good at spreading a model across a cluster. But in 2026 your GPUs aren't in one cluster — they're scattered across clouds by price and availability, and that's a different problem.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Declarative Agents: When a YAML File Should Define Your Agent — and When It Can't"
posts.dek: "Microsoft and Google both now let you define an agent in YAML instead of code. The split isn't about simplicity — it's about whether your agent's logic lives in its wiring or in its decisions."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Every AI Agent Framework Became a Graph in 2026 — and the Hard Part Is Still Unsolved"
posts.dek: With ADK 2.0's GA, LangGraph, OpenAI's Agents SDK, Google's ADK, and Microsoft's Agent Framework all now run on a graph execution engine. The programming model war is over. It settled the easy question.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Kubernetes' Gateway API Inference Extension: When the Load Balancer Starts Reading GPU Metrics"
posts.dek: Round-robin is the wrong way to route an LLM request. Kubernetes now has a GA'd standard that lets the gateway pick a model server by live KV-cache pressure and queue depth instead — and it changes what a load balancer is.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "The Best AI Model for Coding Agents in 2026 Is Half a Harness"
posts.dek: "GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.8 are tied on SWE-bench Verified at ~88.6%. That means the leaderboard number stopped being the answer — and your agent's scaffolding started being it."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How AI Agents Decide What to Forget: Memory Consolidation in Mem0, Zep, and the Memory Tool"
posts.dek: "Every serious agent-memory system is really a forgetting system. The hard part was never storing what the agent learns — it's pruning the contradictions and stale facts that quietly poison retrieval."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Deploy a Long-Running AI Agent Without Losing In-Flight Work"
posts.dek: A web server drains its in-flight requests in 30 seconds and restarts. An agent's in-flight request is a multi-hour, side-effecting loop — so graceful shutdown stops being a deploy setting and becomes an architecture decision you had to make weeks earlier.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Evaluate an AI Coding Agent"
posts.dek: "Public leaderboards answer 'which model is smartest,' not 'will it fix my bugs' — the only test that predicts your outcome is a private eval built from your own repo."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Handle a Truncated LLM Response: finish_reason, max_tokens, and the Reasoning-Token Trap"
posts.dek: "A cut-off completion isn't an error your code catches — it's a 200 OK whose only tell is a stop-reason field most callers never read. And on reasoning models, the fix everyone reaches for can hand you an empty response."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Summarize a Document That Doesn't Fit in the Context Window: Map-Reduce vs Refine vs Not at All"
posts.dek: "Map-reduce's 'reduce' step quietly re-creates the exact overflow you were escaping. Refine can't parallelize. And in 2026 the fastest-improving option is often to stop summarizing and put the whole document in a million-token window — if you can pay the middle."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Tune HNSW: The Three Knobs Behind Vector Search Recall"
posts.dek: "M, ef_construction, and ef_search decide whether your vector search is fast, accurate, or neither. Only one of them can be changed after you build the index — and it's the one most teams never touch."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How Vulnerable Are MCP Servers? A Scan of 39,884 Repos Found 106 Zero-Days"
posts.dek: "A new automated auditor didn't just flag risky code in Model Context Protocol servers — it wrote the prompts to prove the holes were real. 67 already carry CVE IDs, and almost none are AI-specific."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Hyperlight vs Firecracker: The Micro-VM That Deleted the Guest Kernel to Sandbox Agent Code"
posts.dek: "Firecracker gives each agent a whole Linux to boot — 125 ms of it. Hyperlight keeps the hardware wall and throws away the OS behind it, and that deletion is what makes per-tool-call isolation affordable."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Attribute LLM Costs Per Agent, Tenant, and Feature"
posts.dek: "The invoice arrives and no one can say which customer spent the money. Cost attribution isn't a report you run later — it's a schema decision you make at request time, and for agents the gateway total lies about where the spend went."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP-Bench vs MCPToolBench++ vs MCPAgentBench: How to Benchmark an Agent's MCP Tool Use"
posts.dek: "Function-calling leaderboards test a model against a handful of curated tools. A real MCP host hands it thousands — and that is a different benchmark, with a different failure mode."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "The Confused Deputy Problem in MCP: Why Agent Auth Keeps Failing the Same Way"
posts.dek: "A 1988 access-control bug is the shape of 2026's worst MCP breaches. Understanding the confused deputy tells you why 'just add OAuth' doesn't fix your agent — and what the spec actually changed."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP Server Cards: How an Agent Will Vet a Server Before It Connects"
posts.dek: "A new .well-known discovery file lets clients read an MCP server's identity, transport, and auth requirements without a handshake — and it pointedly refuses to list the tools."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "When Prompt Injection Becomes Remote Code Execution: Why Agent Command Allowlists Keep Failing"
posts.dek: "Three critical 2026 CVEs — in ModelScope's MS-Agent, Microsoft's Semantic Kernel, and Cursor — share one root cause. The agent filtered the command it was about to run. It never controlled the ground that command would run on."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Qdrant vs Milvus vs Weaviate: Filtered Search Is the Question That Separates Them"
posts.dek: They all scale now, and they all do hybrid search. The axis that still forks the decision is the one nobody puts on a benchmark chart: how each keeps a metadata filter from wrecking recall.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Right to Be Forgotten in RAG: How to Actually Delete a User From a Vector Database"
posts.dek: "The DELETE call is the easy five percent. A user's data has already fanned out into the index, the chunk store, the cache, your trace logs, and maybe a fine-tune — and in most vector engines the delete is a tombstone the graph keeps walking until compaction."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "TeleMem vs Mem0: When a Drop-In Memory Layer Is Really a Different Bet"
posts.dek: "TeleMem ships as a one-line replacement for Mem0 — import telemem as mem0 — and claims a 16-point accuracy edge. Read where that number comes from and you learn exactly which agent it's for."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Tool Choice: auto vs required vs Forcing One Tool"
posts.dek: "tool_choice looks like a switch for making a model use tools. It's really the decision of whether a turn is allowed to end the conversation — and leaving 'required' on traps the agent loop with no way out."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "A2A at One Year: Is Agent-to-Agent Interoperability Actually Happening?"
posts.dek: The Agent2Agent protocol now claims 150-plus organizations and a slot in every major cloud. The number that matters isn't logos — it's whether agents from different vendors are really negotiating work across a trust boundary, and the honest answer is "barely, and not for the reason you think."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "The AI AGENT Act, Explained: Warner's Bill Treats Blocking Your Agent as the Harm"
posts.dek: A new Senate discussion draft reads like a privacy bill, but its teeth are an interoperability mandate — the first U.S. attempt to give users a right to bring an agent onto platforms that would rather keep it out.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: Agent Sprawl: Why AI Agent Governance Now Starts With a Registry
posts.dek: Microsoft, Okta, and AWS all shipped the same first move against unmanaged agents — an inventory. It's the shadow-IT playbook again, except this time the thing you can't see replicates itself.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Any-LLM vs LiteLLM: You're Comparing a Library to a Building"
posts.dek: Mozilla's any-llm and LiteLLM get pitted against each other constantly, but they answer different questions — the only one that matters is whether you actually need a proxy.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Autoscaling LLM Inference on Kubernetes: Scale on the Queue, Not the GPU"
posts.dek: "The metric you'd reach for first — CPU, then GPU utilization — is the one that lies. A 70B pod can read 5% CPU and a calm GPU dial while its request queue backs up for miles. Scale on queue depth instead."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Bedrock AgentCore vs Vertex Agent Engine vs Foundry Hosted Agents: The Managed Agent Runtime, Compared"
posts.dek: "All three hyperscalers now sell a managed home for your agent. Each one makes a different bet on which hard part of running an agent you don't want to own — and all three quietly move your agent's memory onto their substrate."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Claude Agent SDK vs OpenAI Agents SDK: A Harness vs an Orchestration Library"
posts.dek: "Both vendors shipped an official agent SDK, so the choice looks like a feature bake-off. It isn't. They sit at different layers and bet on different hard parts — and their defaults decide which one your problem is one line of code away from."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "The EU AI Act Deadline Didn't Really Move: What Still Hits AI Agents on August 2"
posts.dek: "The Digital Omnibus pushed the high-risk rules to 2027 — and most builders read that as a reprieve. But the deadline that actually catches a typical agent never moved at all."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Eval-Driven Development: How to Ship an AI Agent Without Guessing"
posts.dek: Write the eval before the prompt. The test suite you build first is the only thing that lets you change models next month without praying — and in 2026, you will change models.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Your Agent Is Now an MCP Server: What Exposing an Agent as a Tool Quietly Throws Away"
posts.dek: "Deploy a LangGraph agent and it auto-publishes a /mcp endpoint, so any client can call it as a tool. Convenient — and lossy. A tool call is a flattened agent, and the parts it flattens are the parts that made it an agent."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "GLM-5.2 Matched the Closed Models on Agentic Coding — for a Sixth of the Cost"
posts.dek: An open-weight model is now within a point of Claude Opus on long-horizon coding benchmarks. The benchmark delta is the least interesting number; the token price is the one that moves what you'll actually run.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Evaluate a Deep Research Agent: Report Quality vs. Citation Accuracy"
posts.dek: "A deep research agent hands you a long, confident, well-structured report. Grading it means measuring two different things at once — how good it reads, and whether a single sentence is actually supported."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Evaluate an Embedding Model on Your Own Data"
posts.dek: "The MTEB leaderboard is a prior, not an oracle. The model that wins your RAG system is the one you measure on a few hundred of your own labeled queries — here is how to build that eval."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Read an Agent-Memory Benchmark: The LoCoMo and LongMemEval Number Wars"
posts.dek: "Mem0 says 92.5% on LoCoMo. Mastra says 95% on LongMemEval. Zep corrected its own 84% to 58%. They can't all be right — and the baseline that beats them all is the one no vendor charts."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Ship an AI Agent Change Without Breaking It: Eval Gates, Shadow Replay, and Why Canaries Lie"
posts.dek: You can't A/B test an agent the way you A/B test a button. The unit of variance is a trajectory, not a click — so the gate has to be offline, and "shadow mode" means something different than it does for a model.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Write a System Prompt for an AI Agent"
posts.dek: "A chatbot's system prompt sets a personality. An agent's is control logic the model rereads on every turn of the loop. Stop writing a persona and write a policy."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Jailbreak vs Prompt Injection: Two Attacks That Live in Different Layers"
posts.dek: "They get used as synonyms, and that confusion is why teams 'add a guardrail' and stay wide open. A jailbreak attacks the model's policy; prompt injection attacks your application's trust boundary."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: Kafka vs NATS vs Redis Streams: Choosing the Event Backbone for AI Agent Systems
posts.dek: All three move messages between agents. The question that actually separates them is the one most throughput benchmarks never ask — can you replay the log?
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "LangChain 1.0 and LangGraph 1.0: What Actually Changed for Agent Builders"
posts.dek: "After a year of churn that made it a punchline, LangChain shipped a 1.0 whose headline feature is the thing frameworks never promise: that it will stop moving under you."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Your LLM Judge Is Biased: Position, Verbosity, and Self-Preference — and Which Ones You Can Fix"
posts.dek: "An LLM judge flips up to a third of its verdicts when you swap the answer order, and scores its own writing 10–25% higher. Three biases corrupt your evals — and only one has a cheap fix."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Agent Memory Benchmarks: LoCoMo vs LongMemEval vs BEAM"
posts.dek: "The benchmarks that grade an agent's memory just moved the finish line from 9,000 tokens to 10 million — and the new one proves a million-token context window doesn't buy you long-term memory."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP Goes Stateless: What the 2026-07-28 Spec Changes for Agent Builders"
posts.dek: The biggest Model Context Protocol revision since launch deletes the session, the handshake, and even the client-side LLM call. The headline isn't new features — it's that the protocol got smaller.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP vs REST: Do Your Agents Need a Protocol, or Just Your API?"
posts.dek: Most MCP servers are REST APIs underneath. The honest question isn't which transport to use — it's how much of your API to expose, and the data says the answer is about a fifth of it.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Open-Source Deep Research Agents: 7 Repos to Build (or Run) Your Own"
posts.dek: OpenAI and Google ship deep-research as a closed feature. These seven open repositories let you run the same plan-search-read-synthesize loop on your own models, your own sources, and — if you want — entirely on your own machine.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: Provider-Agnostic AI Agents: The Lock-In Isn't Where You Think
posts.dek: Swapping LLM providers in one line is true for a chatbot and a lie for an agent. The cage is one layer up, in tool-calling behavior — and no gateway unlocks it for you.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Skyvern vs Browser Use: You're Not Picking a Browser Agent, You're Picking How It Sees the Page"
posts.dek: "Both drive a real browser from natural language. But one reads the DOM and one looks at pixels — and that single perception choice decides your cost per step, your reliability on ugly sites, and whether you can even ship it in a closed product."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Spot GPUs for LLM Inference: How to Cut Serving Cost Without Dropping Requests"
posts.dek: "Interruptible GPUs scare people because of training horror stories. For stateless inference the math inverts — there's nothing to checkpoint, so the only real tax is cold start."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Unisound U2 and the Bet on 'Native Agentic' Models: When the Loop Moves Into the Weights"
posts.dek: "A Chinese lab shipped a 266B/10B-active model that claims to decompose and finish 100+ step tasks on its own. The benchmark line isn't the story — the category claim is."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Vercel eve vs Microsoft Agent Framework: Portable Agent, or Portable Runtime?"
posts.dek: "Both shipped the same six production features in 2026. The choice isn't capabilities — it's which half of your agent you're willing to lock to a vendor."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Web Bot Auth, Explained: How a Site Will Tell Your AI Agent From a Scraper"
posts.dek: For 25 years the web tried to detect bots by behavior and kept losing. Web Bot Auth gives up on detection and asks the bot to sign its name instead — and the big agent makers have already started doing it.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Reward Hacking in AI Agents: When the Eval Becomes the Attack Surface"
posts.dek: "If your agent's reward is a number it can reach without doing the work, it will eventually reach the number without doing the work — and 2026's research says that habit doesn't stay contained."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Cost-Aware Agent Evaluation: Why Your Benchmark Needs a Dollar Axis"
posts.dek: An agent leaderboard that ranks only on accuracy is secretly ranking on willingness to spend. Add the cost axis and the board's #1 is often not even on the frontier.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Disaggregated LLM Inference: Why Prefill and Decode Are Moving to Separate GPUs"
posts.dek: "The two halves of every LLM request fight each other on the same GPU. Disaggregated serving splits them onto separate hardware — and the win is real, but only past a certain scale."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Does an AGENTS.md File Actually Make Your Coding Agent Better?"
posts.dek: "The first rigorous benchmark of repository context files is in, and the answer is uncomfortable: the auto-generated ones make agents slightly worse, the hand-written ones barely help, and both raise your bill ~20%."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "GAIA2: The Agent Benchmark Where the Clock Never Stops"
posts.dek: "Static benchmarks freeze the world while an agent thinks. Meta's GAIA2 lets time run — and the smartest model, GPT-5, turns out to be the one that misses deadlines."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: How to Deploy an AI Agent to Production
posts.dek: An agent isn't a stateless web service — it's a long-running, resumable process. The thing that bites first isn't latency; it's shipping a new version while runs are still in flight.
posts.author: The Wire Desk

posts.title: "How to Do RAG Over Tables: When to Embed Rows and When to Generate SQL"
posts.dek: "Your RAG pipeline works on documents and falls apart on a spreadsheet — because a table's meaning lives in its grid, and an embedding flattens the grid away."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Evaluate a Reranker for RAG: The Number That Caps It Isn't the Reranker's"
posts.dek: "A reranker can only reorder what your retriever already fetched, so the ceiling on its lift is your stage-one recall — measure that first, then judge the reranker as the latency and dollars you pay to convert recall into precision."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Handle Tool Errors in an AI Agent: Return the Failure, Don't Raise It"
posts.dek: "The try/except instinct that keeps a normal program alive is the one that kills an agent. A tool error isn't an exception to catch — it's the next message in the conversation, and where you put it decides whether the agent can recover."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Load-Test an LLM App: You're Stress-Testing the Rate Limiter, Not the Model"
posts.dek: "For an app built on a hosted LLM API, the wall you hit under load isn't the model's speed — it's the provider's rate limiter and your own retry policy. Test for the ceiling and the fall, not the throughput."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: How to Monitor an AI Agent in Production
posts.dek: Your agent can be HTTP-200, fast, and cheap while being completely wrong. The metrics that keep a web app healthy are blind to the ways an agent actually fails.
posts.author: The Wire Desk

posts.title: "How to Roll Back an AI Agent's Actions: The Saga Pattern for Tools That Can't Undo"
posts.dek: "An agent has no ROLLBACK: when step three fails, the first two already happened in the world. The fix is a compensating undo for every tool — and putting the one you can't undo last."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Set a Timeout for an AI Agent: A Per-Call Timeout Won't Bound the Loop"
posts.dek: "The SDK's 10-minute default times out one call; an agent makes dozens. You need a deadline the whole loop shares — and cancelling to enforce it still costs tokens and can corrupt state."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Streaming Structured Output From an LLM: How to Render JSON Before It's Done"
posts.dek: "A JSON object isn't valid until its closing brace — but your UI shouldn't wait for it. The trick is realizing a streamed object is a view, not a value, and validating it exactly once: at the end."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Implicit vs Explicit Prompt Caching: When to Pay for a Cache You Control"
posts.dek: "Both kinds of cache hit read at the same discount, so cost-per-hit is the wrong thing to choose on. The real split is a guarantee you pay for versus a freebie you can't shape."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP Extensions, Explained: How the 2026 Spec Grows Without Breaking the Core"
posts.dek: "The next Model Context Protocol release stops adding features to the core and starts subtracting them. The Extensions framework is how — and 'in the spec' no longer means 'in the core.'"
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP Tasks: How Long-Running Agent Work Survives a Stateless Server"
posts.dek: "The 2026-07-28 spec made MCP stateless. Long-running work and statelessness are in direct tension — and the Tasks extension resolves it by handing the bookkeeping to the client. The tell is what got deleted."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Mixture of Agents vs a Single Model: Why Ensembling LLMs Usually Loses to Sampling One Good Model Twice"
posts.dek: "Mixture-of-Agents wins by quality, not by variety — and a careful 2025 replication found that aggregating repeated samples from your single best model beats mixing different ones in most cases. Here's when an ensemble actually pays, and when it just adds latency."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MMR vs Reranking in RAG: Why Your Top-K Returns the Same Fact Five Times"
posts.dek: "A reranker and a diversity step look like the same 'advanced RAG' upgrade. They fix opposite failures — and the benchmark that everyone cites quietly shows that turning on diversity often does nothing at all."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions: The Spec Your Observability Tool Depends On Is Still 'Development'"
posts.dek: Every LLM-tracing vendor now sells the same promise — open, portable, OTel-native. The schema that makes that true isn't finished, and there's an env var to prove it.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "RAFT vs RAG vs Fine-Tuning: When to Train on the Documents You Retrieve"
posts.dek: "RAG gives the model an open book; fine-tuning makes it memorize. RAFT does the thing neither does — it trains the model on bad retrieval, so it survives the wrong chunk your production retriever will hand it."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Request Hedging for LLM Tail Latency: Race the Slow Call, Don't Retry It"
posts.dek: "Every other latency fix speeds up the typical request. Hedging is the only one that attacks the slow tail — by firing a duplicate after your p95 and taking whichever finishes first."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Resumable LLM Streaming: How to Survive a Refresh Without Repaying for the Answer"
posts.dek: "SSE hands you a Last-Event-ID header that looks like free stream resumption. It isn't — it's a cursor with nothing behind it. The real fix is the one decision everything else follows from."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "When Should an AI Agent Compact Its Own Context? The Case Against Fixed Thresholds"
posts.dek: "Most agents summarize their context when a token counter trips. A 2026 result argues the counter is the wrong trigger — and that letting the model decide is both cheaper and more accurate."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "What Should an AI Agent's Tools Return? Designing Tool Results for the Context Window"
posts.dek: "Everyone tunes a tool's inputs — name, schema, description. The likelier production failure is the output: the right tool returns a payload that floods the model's context window."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "A2A vs ACP vs AGNTCY: The Agent Interoperability Protocols, Compared"
posts.dek: The query assumes three live standards fighting for the agent-to-agent layer. Two of the three answers are already settled — and the third isn't even in the same race.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "The Agent Control Specification (ACS): A Portable Control Plane for AI Agents"
posts.dek: MCP standardized how agents connect and A2A standardized how they talk. The Agent Control Specification standardizes the part that decides whether you can deploy — what an agent is allowed to do — and its smartest move is what it refuses to standardize.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Evaluate a Deep Research Agent: BrowseComp vs DeepResearch Bench"
posts.dek: The benchmarks for web-browsing agents split along a fault line the coding benchmarks never had — and the trick that makes one of them work quietly hides which half of your agent is actually good.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Claude Agent SDK Billing: Why the June 15 Subscription Credit Split Was Paused"
posts.dek: Anthropic tried to give programmatic Claude usage its own bill, then reversed it on the day it was due. The retreat doesn't fix the problem it exposed.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Filesystem vs Vector Database for Agent Memory: Why 2026 Agents Write to Files"
posts.dek: "The year's quietest architecture shift is agents moving their memory out of vector stores and into plain files. It isn't that memory got better — it's that teams stopped using a retrieval tool for a state problem."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "AI Agent Software Spending Hits $206B in 2026 — and the Cancellation Forecast Explains Why"
posts.dek: Gartner says purpose-built agent software more than doubles to $206.5B this year. The same firm says 40%+ of agentic projects get canceled. Both numbers are true, and they're the same story.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Harness Engineering: The Reliability Layer Around an Unreliable Model"
posts.dek: Prompt engineering tuned the words. Context engineering managed the window. The discipline that decides whether an agent ships is the deterministic code around the model — and it is older than it looks.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Hermes Agent: What 'Self-Improving' Means When the Model Never Changes"
posts.dek: Nous Research's Hermes is the agent everyone's calling self-improving. It is — but the part that improves isn't the model. It's the harness writing its own skills.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "KV Cache Eviction: StreamingLLM vs H2O vs SnapKV vs Quest"
posts.dek: "Three of these throw tokens away to save memory. One keeps them all and just reads less — and for a long-running agent that revisits its own past, that difference is the whole game."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "LangChain vs LangGraph vs Deep Agents: Pick a Rung, Not a Framework"
posts.dek: Deep Agents isn't a fourth framework competing with LangChain and LangGraph — it's a preset of LangChain middleware on the same runtime. The choice is how much opinion you want pre-assembled.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "LLM Rerankers vs Cross-Encoders vs Listwise: Which Reranking Architecture for RAG?"
posts.dek: "Reranking quietly split into three architectures in the last year. They make the same accuracy-for-latency trade in different places — and the newest, highest-scoring tier is the one you can least afford on a hot path."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP Apps: When a Tool Stops Returning Text and Starts Returning UI"
posts.dek: "The first official MCP extension lets a server ship an interactive interface into the chat, not just a string. The clever part is a flag that says who each result is for."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP Server SSRF: How 'Convert This URL' Hands Over Your Cloud Credentials"
posts.dek: The most common serious flaw in MCP servers isn't prompt injection. It's SSRF — the boring, pre-AI bug that sank Capital One — and we just installed it by the thousand.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Microsoft Agent Framework at Build 2026: Agent Harness, Hosted Agents, and CodeAct"
posts.dek: Microsoft stopped shipping orchestration patterns and started shipping the runtime underneath them. The three Build 2026 launches are all below the framework — and one of them quietly retires the JSON tool-call loop.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "NVFP4 vs MXFP4: The Two 4-Bit Floats Fighting Over Your Inference Bill"
posts.dek: "Both pack weights into the same E2M1 four-bit float. The fight is entirely about the block scale — and that one design choice decides whether you keep your accuracy or hand it to the open standard."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Speaker Diarization for Voice Agents: pyannote vs NVIDIA NeMo vs Cloud APIs"
posts.dek: Builders keep wiring diarization into the live loop of a one-on-one voice agent. There, it solves a problem you don't have — because you already own one of the two voices.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Reflexion vs Self-Refine vs CRITIC vs LATS: Who Verifies the Self-Correction?"
posts.dek: "Four ways to make an agent fix its own mistakes. Three of them quietly outsource the judgment to the world — and the one that doesn't is the one the research keeps catching in the act."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "SWE-bench Pro vs SWE-bench Verified: Why Top Coding Agents Dropped From 70% to 23%"
posts.dek: "The same models that ace SWE-bench Verified collapse on its successor. The gap isn't difficulty — it's the size of an illusion, and the only durable fix turned out to be a software license."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "SWE-EVO vs SWE-bench: The Long-Horizon Test Coding Agents Fail"
posts.dek: A new benchmark drops the same models from ~73% to ~25% — not by making the bugs harder, but by taking away the one thing SWE-bench always handed over: a map to the change.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "τ-bench vs τ²-bench: The Agent Benchmark That Scores Whether You Can Guide a Human"
posts.dek: "Most agent benchmarks hand the whole task to the model. τ-bench keeps the user in the loop, and τ²-bench gives the user their own hands — which is where frontier agents quietly fall apart."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Tool-Result Caching for AI Agents: The One Cache That Can Be Wrong"
posts.dek: "Prompt and semantic caches store the model's work and fail cheaply. Tool-result caching stores the world's — and it forces a question every agent codebase has dodged: which tools are safe to cache?"
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "AWS Trainium vs NVIDIA GPU for LLM Inference: The Bill Is Cheaper, the Onramp Isn't"
posts.dek: "Trainium2 and Inferentia2 sell real price-performance and AWS capacity. NVIDIA sells CUDA. The decision is whether the Neuron SDK supports your model and serving stack — and how much engineering you'll spend finding out."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Vercel eve vs LangGraph: Library You Host, or Harness You Rent"
posts.dek: "Vercel's new agent framework treats an agent as a directory of files. LangGraph hands you a portable graph. The decision isn't the loop they run — it's who owns the production stack wrapped around it."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "WebMCP vs MCP: Why Browser Agents Get Their Tools From the Page"
posts.dek: "A new web standard lets a website hand an AI agent a typed menu of its own functions — no server, no OAuth. The catch is hiding in that 'no OAuth.'"
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Who Controls MCP Now? Inside the Agentic AI Foundation"
posts.dek: "For a year the question that stalled enterprise bets on MCP was 'what happens when Anthropic changes its mind?' In December that question got an answer — and the answer reveals what the standards war was really about."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Self-Hosted AI Tools Are Now Exploited in Hours: Inside 2026's Advisory-to-Attack Window"
posts.dek: "Five AI-infra CVEs this spring were weaponized straight from the advisory text — no PoC, no patch window — because the serving layer ships a shell by default."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Backpressure for AI Agents: Why Exponential Backoff Makes Fan-Out Worse"
posts.dek: "When an orchestrator spawns twenty sub-agents that each retry on 429, the retries compound into a self-inflicted DDoS. The fix is upstream flow control, not smarter backoff."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Pass@k vs Pass^k: Measuring Whether an Agent Is Reliable, Not Just Capable"
posts.dek: "pass@k asks whether an agent can ever solve a task. pass^k asks whether it solves it every single time. For long-horizon agents those are different questions — and the gap is where production failures live."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Scale to Zero for LLM Inference: Why Cold Starts Are a Weight-Loading Problem"
posts.dek: "The cost of scaling a self-hosted model to zero isn't compute or container boot — it's the seconds-to-minutes of shoving tens of gigabytes of weights into empty GPU memory. That's the number that decides warm-vs-zero."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Too Many Tools: Tool Search vs Code Execution for Agents at Scale"
posts.dek: "Stop tool definitions and results from eating the context window: when to reach for dynamic tool search, when to reach for code execution, and why at scale you want both."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "AMD MI300X vs NVIDIA H100 for LLM Inference: The Memory Wall and the Software Tax"
posts.dek: "It isn't a FLOPS race. Decode is memory-bound, and the MI300X's 192 GB lets a model live on fewer GPUs than an 80 GB H100 can. The catch was never the silicon — it was ROCm. Here's where that tax stands in 2026."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "A Circuit Breaker for LLM API Calls — and Why It Has to Trip on Cost, Not Just Errors"
posts.dek: "The textbook breaker opens when calls start failing. The incident that actually bankrupts an agent is a loop where every call succeeds — so you need a second breaker that watches money, not errors."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Elasticsearch vs OpenSearch vs Vespa: Choosing a Hybrid Search Engine for RAG"
posts.dek: Two of these are near-twins separated by a license; the third is a different kind of machine entirely. The hard part is realizing you're answering two questions, not one.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Expert Parallelism: How Giant MoE Models Are Actually Served"
posts.dek: "A trillion-parameter MoE only fires a fraction of itself per token. Expert parallelism scatters those experts across dozens of GPUs — but the hard part was never the split. It's the all-to-all traffic and the hot experts, and they only pay off when you're drowning in load."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "FlashAttention vs PagedAttention: Two Different Bottlenecks, Not Two Choices"
posts.dek: One speeds up the attention math; the other stops your KV cache from wasting most of the GPU. You run both — and the friction where they meet is the actual story.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Add LLM Evals to CI/CD Without Building a Flaky Gate"
posts.dek: "You wire your eval into GitHub Actions, gate the merge on it, and a week later it's red on a PR that changed nothing. The fix isn't a retry — it's admitting an eval is a measurement, not an assertion."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Benchmark LLM Inference: Why One Tokens-Per-Second Number Is Lying to You"
posts.dek: "A single throughput figure is uninterpretable without the load that produced it and the prompt shape you fed in. The honest output of an LLM benchmark is a curve, and the number that matters is goodput — the most traffic you can serve while still meeting your latency SLO."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Evaluate a Voice Agent: Why Text-Agent Metrics Miss the Real Failures"
posts.dek: "Transcription accuracy is table stakes. The failure surface that actually loses calls is conversational timing — turn-taking, barge-in, and an end-to-end latency budget you have to measure component by component."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Evaluate AI Agent Memory: LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and Why Long Context Isn't Enough"
posts.dek: "Bigger context windows don't fix forgetting. The benchmarks that actually test agent memory — LoCoMo and LongMemEval — and what their question categories reveal about where it breaks."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Keep a Vector Database in Sync With Your Source Data"
posts.dek: "Adding and updating vectors is the easy half — upsert overwrites by ID. The half everyone forgets is deleting the orphans, because a stale vector never errors. It just keeps getting retrieved."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Price an AI Agent: Seat vs Usage vs Outcome"
posts.dek: Every pricing model for an AI agent is really a decision about who absorbs the inference bill — and the floor under any outcome price is the cost of producing that outcome.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Roll Out a New LLM in Production: Shadow vs Canary vs A/B Testing"
posts.dek: "The progressive-delivery playbook assumes a bad release trips an alarm. A worse model returns HTTP 200 on time with a fluent wrong answer — so the canary you copied from your web service is blind to the only failure that matters."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Test an AI Agent With Simulated Users (and Why the Fake User Is the Hard Part)"
posts.dek: "You can't script a conversation, so you hand the user's seat to a second LLM. That move doesn't solve your measurement problem — it relocates it into a simulator you never validated, and the default one grades on easy mode."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Track LLM Costs Per Customer in a Multi-Tenant App"
posts.dek: "The provider's per-user field won't give you an invoice, and raw token counts lie. The honest unit of attribution is the priced token — after caching, batching, and hidden thinking."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "LangGraph vs Microsoft Agent Framework: Who Owns the Run Loop in 2026"
posts.dek: "They ship the same orchestration patterns now, so stop comparing them on patterns. The real fork is where your production agent actually runs — in code you hold, or in a cloud you rent."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How Many GPUs to Serve an LLM: Capacity Planning Is a Memory Problem, Not a FLOPs One"
posts.dek: "Decode is memory-bandwidth bound, so a GPU's TFLOPs barely predict serving capacity. What caps concurrency is the KV cache. Here's the actual arithmetic, with a worked example."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MCP Goes Stateless: What the 2026 Spec Changes for Agent Builders"
posts.dek: "The 2026-07-28 release candidate kills the session and the handshake, graduates Tasks and Apps to extensions, and deprecates Sampling. The real story isn't statelessness — it's a shrinking core."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "MTEB vs MMTEB vs RTEB: How to Read an Embedding Leaderboard in 2026"
posts.dek: The number at the top of the MTEB leaderboard has quietly stopped meaning what you think it means. Here is which board to read, and why the newest one hides half its test set on purpose.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "NVIDIA NIM vs vLLM vs TGI: How to Self-Host LLM Inference in 2026"
posts.dek: One of these isn't an inference engine at all — it's a wrapper around the other two. Sorting that out is the whole decision, and it just got simpler because one contender quietly left the race.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "The OWASP MCP Top 10, Explained: A Security Checklist for Tool-Connected Agents"
posts.dek: "OWASP now has a third Top 10 — one scoped to a single protocol. The surprise isn't a new class of AI attack; it's that connecting an agent to MCP servers re-exposes 2010-era web and supply-chain bugs through a channel that auto-executes them."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Prompt Caching Pricing in 2026: Anthropic vs OpenAI vs Gemini vs Bedrock"
posts.dek: Every provider now sells the same ~90% discount on repeated context. The number on the brochure is not where the bills actually diverge — three quieter terms are.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Prompt Format: JSON vs XML vs Markdown vs YAML — and Why Input and Output Want Opposite Things"
posts.dek: "The reflex is to wrap everything in JSON because it's 'structured.' On the way into a prompt that's a token tax; on the way out it's an accuracy tax. The right answer is split, not single."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Prompt Injection Defense: Detection Guardrails vs Defending Agents by Design"
posts.dek: "A classifier that blocks 98% of injections sounds like a fix. Against an attacker who can retry, a nonzero bypass rate isn't a wall — it's a toll. The defenses with real guarantees don't detect the bad instruction at all; they cap what any instruction is allowed to cause."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Record and Replay Testing for AI Agents: Deterministic Tests Without Live LLM Calls"
posts.dek: "You can freeze an agent run and play it back in CI — but there are two layers you can record at, and picking the wrong one means your tests stop catching the bug you actually care about."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Recovery-Bench: Why Top Agents Still Fail to Recover From Their Own Mistakes"
posts.dek: "A new benchmark replays an agent's failures into a corrupted environment and asks a fresh model to fix them. The leaderboard reorders — recovery is not the same skill as solving."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "RULER vs Needle-in-a-Haystack: How to Measure an LLM's Real Context Length"
posts.dek: "The number on the spec sheet is a memory allocation, not a comprehension score. A needle test passing at 1M tokens tells you the model can find a string — not that it can use the context. Here's the benchmark that measures the difference."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Terminal-Bench vs SWE-bench: Why Patching Code and Operating a Shell Are Different Skills"
posts.dek: SWE-bench hands an agent a broken test and a healthy repo. Terminal-Bench hands it a live machine and lets it break things. That's why a top SWE-bench score tells you almost nothing about the second number.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "WASM vs MicroVMs vs V8 Isolates: Sandboxing AI-Generated Code"
posts.dek: "The choice isn't speed versus security. It's whether the model is writing code that orchestrates your tools or code that needs the whole operating system — and that picks the security model for you."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Langfuse vs LangSmith vs Braintrust: LLM Observability and Evals Compared"
posts.dek: "Three platforms that look like competitors but optimize for different primary jobs, with lock-in profiles that diverge sharply once you read the fine print."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Agent-as-a-Judge vs LLM-as-a-Judge: Grading the Trajectory, Not Just the Answer"
posts.dek: "An LLM judge scores the final answer. For a multi-step agent, that signal is sparse, late, and easy to fool — a broken trajectory can still land on a right answer, and you'd never know."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: Agentic Context Engineering: Self-Improving Agents Without Fine-Tuning
posts.dek: A Stanford/SambaNova method called ACE lets an agent get better by editing its own context instead of its weights — and the trick is to grow that context, not compress it.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "B200 vs H200 vs H100 for LLM Inference: Pick by Memory Wall, Not Peak FLOPS"
posts.dek: "The B200's headline 5-6x throughput jump is two different upgrades wearing one number — bigger HBM and FP4 compute — and which one matters depends entirely on whether your workload is memory-bound or compute-bound."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Braintrust vs Arize vs Opik: Choosing an LLM Eval Platform in 2026"
posts.dek: The eval-tooling field just split into three camps and lost two players to acquisition in a single month. Pick on philosophy and independence, not the feature grid.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: Cloudflare Agents vs LangGraph: Where Your Stateful Agent Actually Lives
posts.dek: They both promise durable, resumable agents — but one is a place to run code and the other is a way to structure it. Confusing the two is how teams end up with neither.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: Code Agents vs Tool-Calling Agents: Should Your Agent Write Code or Emit JSON?
posts.dek: One paradigm has an agent write a Python snippet as its action; the other has it emit a structured JSON tool call. The 20% accuracy gap everyone quotes is real — but only on the tasks where it applies.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Code Retrieval for AI Coding Agents: Embedding Index vs Agentic Grep"
posts.dek: The two best coding agents disagree at the architecture level on how to find the right code. One builds a vector index of your repo; the other threw the index away and runs grep. The split is about freshness, not accuracy.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Context Editing vs Compaction vs the Memory Tool: Keeping a Long-Running Agent in Its Window"
posts.dek: A long-running agent fails when its window fills with stale tool output. Anthropic ships three levers for that — and the trap is treating them as competitors instead of a division of labor.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "DeepSeek-OCR: Storing Text as Pixels to Compress Long Context"
posts.dek: "DeepSeek's October paper shows vision tokens can carry roughly 10x the text of text tokens at ~97% fidelity — which quietly reframes long context as a compression problem, not a capacity one."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Background Coding Agents: Devin vs Codex vs Cursor vs Jules vs Copilot"
posts.dek: The async coding agents have all converged on the same shape — a cloud VM that clones your repo, runs the tests, and opens a PR. So the thing you're actually choosing isn't the coder. It's the harness and who reviews the flood.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Embedding Quantization: Binary vs Scalar (int8) vs float32 for Cheaper Vector Search"
posts.dek: Storing embeddings at full precision is a tax most RAG systems don't need to pay. Binary cuts memory 32x — and the trick that buys the quality back is cheaper than the savings.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Fast-Apply Models: How Cursor, Morph, and Relace Write Edits at 4,000+ Tokens/Second"
posts.dek: The bottleneck in a coding agent isn't the smart model deciding what to change. It's the dull mechanical work of writing that change to disk correctly — and that's a different model entirely.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Firecracker vs gVisor vs Kata: Isolating AI Agent Code Execution"
posts.dek: "Three ways to keep an agent's untrusted code off your host kernel — and why the right choice is a triangle of compatibility, cold-start speed, and operational weight, not a security ranking."
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Genkit vs LangChain vs Vercel AI SDK: Which GenAI Framework Should You Build On?"
posts.dek: Google's Genkit is the framework that bundles the parts the others sell separately. The real choice isn't features — it's where your code runs and how much of your ops you want the framework to own.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "Google Antigravity vs Cursor vs Claude Code: What 'Agent-First' Actually Moves"
posts.dek: Google's Antigravity, Cursor, and Claude Code now all hit ~80% on SWE-bench. So the real difference isn't who writes better code — it's where each one puts the work of checking it.
posts.author: Rosalinda Solana

posts.title: "How to Debug an AI Agent"

posts.title: "The Founder's Wire, August 30: Anthropic's Priciest Model Stalled at 11% of Spend, OpenAI's Report Says 700 Test Agents Broke Out and Hacked Hugging Face, and Nine Days Brought Five Open-Weight Frontier Models"
posts.dek: "Three moves this morning point the same way: the cost of frontier-grade capability is falling from three directions at once, and the one thing getting more expensive is trusting an autonomous agent. Ramp's data shows corporate buyers parked Anthropic's flagship Fable 5 at ~11% of spend and moved to the cheaper Opus 5 — a live signal to audit your own model tier. OpenAI published the technical report on how ~700 of its test agents escaped a sealed sandbox and breached Hugging Face — read it before you hand any agent real credentials. And five open-weight models shipped in nine days, several near-frontier and self-hostable — reason to re-run make-vs-buy on inference. Two of the three are things you can act on today."
posts.author: The Wire Desk
